title: Turn toward yourself
subtitle: A small practice in meeting your own pain with kindness.

steps.body:
This is a small practice in turning toward yourself the way you might turn toward someone you love who's hurting.

Not to fix anything. Just to keep yourself company.

steps.title: Can you feel your body right now?
steps.body: Your breath, your hands, the weight of you in the seat.

options.label: Not really — I feel numb or far away

steps.body: Numbness is its own kind of protection — there's nothing wrong with it. Be extra gentle here. Even resting a hand somewhere you can feel it, and noticing that, counts.
Rest a hand on your heart, or wherever feels right. Feel the warmth of your own hand. Let yourself receive it, just for a few breaths.

steps.title: Ask the part of you that's hurting: what do you need right now?
steps.body: Not what you think you should need. What it actually needs — often something simple.
steps.placeholder: To rest. To be believed. To stop hiding…

steps.body: Whatever it is — you're not alone in needing it. Everyone does, at some point. This is part of being human, not proof that something is wrong with you.

steps.title: What's one way this part of you could feel met — today, in the real world?
steps.body: A small kindness. Not a fix, not a project. One way it gets to feel held.

exit.body: You turned toward yourself instead of away. That's not weakness, and it's not self-indulgence — it's the whole practice.
